newsitem.title: USA: U.S., New Jersey win $30 mln for landfill clean-up.
newsitem.headline: U.S., New Jersey win $30 mln for landfill clean-up.

text.p: The U.S. government and the state of New Jersey reached a $30 million settlement Thursday with almost 300 parties to pay for cleaning up the GEMS landfill in Gloucester Township in New Jersey.

The settlement, ending four years of negotiations with large and small companies and municipal agencies, included 252 parties who dumped small amounts of hazardous waste at the former 60-acre municipal site, the Justice Department said.
The landfill was used from 1969 to 1980 for dumping industrial wastes, such as asbestos, solvents and heavy metals, which polluted groundwater, surface water and soil.
The agreement included a $16.5 million trust to be set up to help extract and treat groundwater.

The Environmental Protection Agency will receive $3.275 million for past clean-up costs at the site. The state will receive $5 million to cover clean-up costs and compensate for the loss of millions of gallons of drinkable water.

Clean-up at the site had been "complicated by several legal and environmental issues, due to the number of parties involved and the presence of rare plants which now will be permanently protected," said Bob Shinn, commissioner of the New Jersey Department of Environmental Protection.
